Salento deep karst aquifer · synthetic test bed

Mapping a groundwater plume from scattered wells

A MODFLOW 6 plume is sampled at 117 real Salento well locations and rebuilt four ways. Physics, machine learning and kriging together give the best map, and they point to where the next wells should go.

  • Wells in the 14 × 14 km area117
  • True plumes tested11
  • Plume outline F1 at 10 yr, hybrid0.86 ± 0.03
  • Same, ordinary kriging0.67 ± 0.16
  • Hybrid beats kriging (10 yr)10 of 11

Approach

A model plume is the only plume whose every cell is known, so it is the fair way to score a mapping method. The workflow applies a hybrid machine-learning approach for groundwater plumes to Salento, using the ArchPy geological model and the real well locations.

01–02Groundwater model

Regional flow at 500 m, then a 50 m local flow and transport model near Lecce.

03Sample the wells

True plume read at 117 wells, 15 % lab error, 0.1 mg/L detection limit.

04Physics prior

The plume a modeller would predict from the regional geology alone.

05Rebuild the plume

Kriging, random forest, prior, and the hybrid of all three.

06Next wells

Add wells where the hybrid is least sure of the plume edge.

07–08Stress test

11 true plumes, then priors built on wrong assumptions.

The groundwater model

One layer for the deep carbonate aquifer (+5 to −150 m a.s.l.). Transmissivity comes from the ArchPy units in that slab: karst limestone carries the flow, and thick Subapennine clay near Taranto and Lecce lowers it. Recharge is 150 mm/yr on permeable outcrops and 20 mm/yr on clay; the sea is a fixed head of 0 m.

Local model settingValue
Grid280 × 280 cells of 50 m, MODFLOW 6 GWF + GWT
Boundaryregional heads on land edges, 0 m at the coast
Sourceconstant 100 mg/L on 100 × 100 m, conservative solute
Effective porosity0.01 (fissured karst)
DispersivityαL 30 m, αT 3 m, TVD advection
Simulated time10 years, monthly periods

Rebuilding the plume from 117 wells

All methods work on log10 concentration. At 3.5 years only 5 wells detect the plume; at 10 years, 28 do. Scores are against the full true plume.

MethodWhat it knows
Kriging (OK)well data and a fitted variogram
Random forest (RF)well data, position along and across the flow, head, regional K
Priorthe physics plume from regional K, rescaled to the data
Hybridphysics plume as the trend, RF correction learned from the wells, kriging of what is left

Where the next wells should go

At 3.5 years, 8 wells are added one at a time. Each is sampled from the true plume and the map is refitted. The hybrid rule picks the cell with the highest P(1 − P), where P is the probability that concentration exceeds 1 mg/L, so wells go to the uncertain plume edge.

Is it luck? 11 true plumes

Ten more true plumes, each with its own random K field, sampled again at the same wells. Mean ± standard deviation; paired Wilcoxon test against kriging.

"Hybrid better than this" counts plumes where the hybrid F1 is higher. Near the source at 10 years the hybrid only ties the prior (7/11, p 0.41): that accuracy comes from the physics.

The original realisation shown above is one of the harder ones: its 3.5-year hybrid F1 is 0.60 against a mean of 0.76.

What if the physics prior is wrong?

The prior is rebuilt with wrong assumptions and the same samples of the 11 plumes are mapped again. F1 of the 1 mg/L plume, mean over 11 plumes. Kriging scores 0.46 at 3.5 years and 0.66 at 10 years with no prior.

Prior built withPrior alone, 3.5 yrHybrid, 3.5 yrPrior alone, 10 yrHybrid, 10 yrVerdict
Correct values0.600.760.730.86reference
Porosity × 2 (plume too short)0.440.740.450.80absorbed
Porosity × ½ (plume too long)0.280.740.730.86absorbed
Dispersivity × 3 (too wide)0.530.770.670.86absorbed
Source 300 m across the flow0.350.470.650.83weak when sparse
All of the above0.150.390.300.76weak when sparse

Porosity and dispersivity errors are corrected by the data: the hybrid stays near 0.75–0.86 while the prior alone collapses. A misplaced source is the weak point. With five detections at 3.5 years the hybrid falls to the level of kriging (0.47 vs 0.46); with 28 detections at 10 years it recovers (0.83, better than kriging in 11 of 11 plumes). The source location is the assumption to get right.

Limits

  • The plume is synthetic. It is a controlled test of mapping methods, not a claim about real contamination near Lecce.
  • One model layer (depth-averaged), fixed aquifer thickness, no seawater density or freshwater–saltwater interface.
  • Regional heads are plausible but not calibrated to measured water levels.
  • Karst is treated as an equivalent porous medium. Conduit flow or a second source were not tested.
  • All true plumes share the same source and the same K statistics.

Mohamed Rewady Abdelall, MSc Geophysics, Università degli Studi di Milano.

Geological model built with ArchPy. Python, flopy, MODFLOW 6, geone, scikit-learn.
